newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Nov 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Nov 29.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO DAILY -- The Hong Kong stock market experienced huge leaps and drops in stock prices yesterday. The Stock Exchange issued letters to six major stock brokers asking for explanations of their unusually heavy buying.
-- Housing had become the number one problem facing the candidates to become the future Hong Kong Chief Executive.
-- SING TAO DAILY -- Taiwan's Nationalist Party has been transferring properties in Hong Kong to a Singapore-registered company to make sure there would be no loss after the handover.
-- WEN WEI PO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin arrived in India. He urged both Chnna and India to develop themselves rapidly and enhance cooperation between them.
-- The Chinese government announced that starting December 1, the yuan would be convertible for current account transactions.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- Easyknit International's chairman said the company would invest HK$150 million to buy three retail spaces and open 10 retail stores in Hong Kong selling its own fashion brand Library.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The Securities and Futures Commission released a series of recommendations designed to provent a repetition of recent scandals that had rocked the financial industry.
-- Coco-Cola Co planned to introduce new products such as flavoured teas in China in the next few months, as part of its agreement with China that allowed the company to expand.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Morgan Stanley Asia's managing director said the rising residential property market risked further government intervention.

-- The Government offered compromises to Hong Kong's massive garments industry over its controversial factory audit checks and its tardiness in handing over export certification needed by manufacturers.
